- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often underestimates the continuation; increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 periods.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1st-3rd day) when sentiment is volatile; add 1-3% buffer to initial forecast.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to lag behind true price; shift forecast 1-2 days ahead with slight upward bias.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.
